Function type for event handlers that take a pointer to an XEvent and return no value. Instances can be stored in arrays such as ev_handler and invoked to process X events. Details of XEvent are external to this header.

Timer node representing a scheduled callback. The field `next` uses the typedef alias `fehtimer` (a pointer alias to this struct), implying an intrusive singly linked list. Alias type for a pointer to struct __fehtimer, used as the list node type for timers. Because the typedef line is missing here, treat this as an inferred alias; if not actually defined in this header, include the proper typedef in a shared header.

functions.name: gib_list_new
functions.description: Create a new list instance. The exact semantics (returning a newly allocated node vs. an empty list sentinel) are not documented here; typical usage is to call this to obtain a list you can add elements to. Details such as whether the returned list initially contains a node with NULL data or represents an empty list are unknown from this header.
requirements: Caller must eventually release the list with gib_list_free or gib_list_free_and_data to avoid leaks (inferred).
Not thread-safe unless documented elsewhere (unknown).

functions.name: gib_list_free
functions.description: Free all nodes in the list l. Based on the presence of gib_list_free_and_data, this function likely frees only the list nodes, not the data pointers stored in them.
requirements: l must be either NULL or a valid list created/managed by this API (inferred).
Data pointers stored in nodes are not freed by this function (inferred).
After this call, any pointers to nodes in l must not be used (inferred).

functions.name: gib_list_add_front
functions.description: Insert a new node containing data at the front (head) of the list rooted at root and return the (possibly new) root.
requirements: root must be NULL or a valid list head managed by this API (inferred).
The data pointer can be NULL; ownership/lifetime of data is managed by the caller (inferred).
Returned pointer should be used as the new root/head (inferred).

functions.name: gib_list_add_end
functions.description: Append a new node containing data to the end (tail) of the list rooted at root and return the (possibly unchanged) root.
requirements: root must be NULL or a valid list head managed by this API (inferred).
The data pointer can be NULL; ownership/lifetime of data is managed by the caller (inferred).
Returned pointer should be used as the current root/head (inferred).

functions.name: gib_list_unlink
functions.description: Detach the node l from the list rooted at root without freeing l, and return the (possibly new) root of the remaining list.
requirements: root must be a valid list (or NULL) managed by this API (inferred).
l must be either NULL or a node that is currently part of the list rooted at root (inferred).
After unlinking, l remains a standalone node; caller is responsible for its disposal (e.g., gib_list_free on that single node or gib_list_remove) (inferred).

functions.name: gib_list_cat
functions.description: Concatenate list l to the end of list root and return the head of the combined list. The links of both lists are adjusted to form a single list.
requirements: root and l must be valid lists (or NULL) managed by this API (inferred).
root and l must not share nodes; concatenating overlapping lists is invalid (inferred).
After concatenation, the l pointer should not be used as a separate list head (inferred).

functions.name: gib_list_length
functions.description: Return the number of nodes in the list l.
requirements: l must be NULL or a valid list managed by this API (inferred).
Return value is non-negative; behavior on extremely large lists may be limited by int range (inferred).

functions.name: gib_list_last
functions.description: Return a pointer to the last (tail) node of list l. If l is empty or NULL, the result may be NULL; exact behavior is not documented here.
requirements: l must be NULL or a valid list managed by this API (inferred).

functions.name: gib_list_first
functions.description: Return a pointer to the first (head) node of list l. If l is empty or NULL, the result may be NULL; exact behavior is not documented here.
requirements: l must be NULL or a valid list managed by this API (inferred).

functions.name: gib_list_jump

functions.description: From node l within the list rooted at root, move num steps in the given direction and return the resulting node. The direction should be FORWARD or BACK as defined by the enum in this header. Behavior when stepping past list ends is not documented here.
requirements: root must be a valid list (or NULL) managed by this API (inferred).
l must be NULL or a node within the list rooted at root (inferred).
direction must be one of the enum values FORWARD or BACK (inferred).
num should be non-negative; negative values are unsupported/undefined (inferred).

functions.name: gib_list_reverse
functions.description: Reverse the order of nodes in the list l and return the new head of the reversed list.
requirements: l must be NULL or a valid list managed by this API (inferred).
All pointers to nodes within l may change relative positions; caller should use the returned head as the new root (inferred).

functions.name: gib_list_randomize
functions.description: Randomize (shuffle) the order of nodes in list and return the new head. Exact shuffling algorithm and randomness quality are not documented here.
requirements: list must be NULL or a valid list managed by this API (inferred).
Caller should use the returned head as the new root (inferred).

functions.name: gib_list_num
functions.description: Return the position/index of node l within the list rooted at root. The indexing base (0 vs 1) is not specified in this header.
requirements: root must be a valid list (or NULL) managed by this API (inferred).
l must be a node within the list rooted at root; otherwise return value/behavior is unspecified here (inferred).

functions.name: gib_list_remove
functions.description: Remove node l from the list rooted at root, freeing that node, and return the (possibly new) head of the remaining list.
requirements: root must be a valid list (or NULL) managed by this API (inferred).
l must be a node currently in the list rooted at root (inferred).
After this call, l must not be used; it is considered freed (inferred).
Data stored in l is likely not freed by this function (inferred from presence of gib_list_free_and_data).

functions.name: gib_list_sort
functions.description: Sort the list using the comparison function cmp and return the new head of the sorted list. The comparator receives two node data pointers and should order them. Stability and sorting algorithm are not documented here.
requirements: list must be NULL or a valid list managed by this API (inferred).
cmp must be a valid function pointer with signature int(void*, void*). It should define a total/strict-weak ordering and return negative/zero/positive analogous to strcmp (inferred).
cmp must safely handle all data pointers stored in the list (inferred).

functions.name: gib_list_sort_merge
functions.signature: gib_list *gib_list_sort_merge(gib_list * l1, gib_list * l2, gib_compare_fn cmp);
functions.description: Merge two lists l1 and l2 into a single sorted list using comparator cmp and return the new head. The function name suggests a merge step of merge sort; exact behavior is not documented here.
requirements: l1 and l2 must be valid lists (or NULL) managed by this API (inferred).
cmp must be a valid function pointer with signature int(void*, void*), consistent across both lists (inferred).
For a correct merged ordering, l1 and l2 should already be sorted according to cmp (inferred).
After merging, original head pointers may no longer represent separate lists (inferred).

functions.name: gib_list_has_more_than_one_item
functions.description: Return a nonzero value if the list rooted at root contains more than one node; otherwise return zero.
requirements: root must be NULL or a valid list managed by this API (inferred).

functions.name: gib_list_free_and_data
functions.description: Free all nodes in the list l and also free each node's data pointer. This implies data must be heap-allocated with a free-compatible allocator.
requirements: l must be NULL or a valid list managed by this API (inferred).
Each node's data pointer must be either NULL or point to memory that can be safely freed via free (inferred).
After this call, any pointers to nodes or their data are invalid (inferred).

functions.name: gib_list_foreach
functions.description: Iterate over the list rooted at root, invoking fe_func for each node with the node pointer and the user-supplied data. Returns a gib_list* (likely the root), but exact return semantics are not documented.
requirements: root must be NULL or a valid list managed by this API (inferred).
fe_func must be a valid function pointer; it will be called once per visited node (inferred).
fe_func should not free or relink the current node unless the implementation documents such modifications as safe (unknown; avoid to be safe).

functions.name: gib_list_find
functions.description: Search the list rooted at root, calling find_func for each node; return the first node for which find_func returns nonzero. Returns NULL if no match is found (inferred).
requirements: root must be NULL or a valid list managed by this API (inferred).
find_func must be a valid predicate function pointer returning an unsigned char truth value (inferred).
find_func must safely handle the node's data and the supplied user data (inferred).

functions.name: gib_list_find_by_data
functions.description: Find and return the first node in root whose stored data matches the provided data. Matching criteria are not documented; likely pointer equality is used.
requirements: root must be NULL or a valid list managed by this API (inferred).
The data pointer is compared according to the implementation; assume pointer equality unless otherwise documented (inferred).

functions.name: gib_string_split
functions.description: Split the input C-string into substrings using the delimiter and return a list of tokens (likely as newly allocated char* strings). Exact tokenization rules (empty tokens, multi-char delimiters, trimming) are not documented here.
requirements: string must be a valid, null-terminated C-string (inferred).
delimiter must be a valid, null-terminated C-string; behavior for empty delimiter is unspecified (inferred).
Caller is responsible for freeing the returned list; if tokens are newly allocated strings, use gib_list_free_and_data to free both nodes and strings (inferred).

functions.name: gib_hash_node_new
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new gib_hash_node that associates a string key with a data pointer. Typically used internally by the hash, but can also be used by callers constructing nodes manually. Ownership semantics for key and data are not documented in this header; whether the key string is copied or the data is merely referenced is unknown.
requirements: key must point to a valid, null-terminated C string.
node memory is allocated by this function; the returned pointer must later be freed with gib_hash_node_free or gib_hash_node_free_and_data to avoid leaks.
data is an arbitrary pointer; whether it may be NULL is not specified.
If gib_hash_node_free_and_data will be used later, the data must be compatible with free (malloc-family) and must not be freed elsewhere.

functions.name: gib_hash_node_free
functions.description: Frees a gib_hash_node previously allocated (e.g., by gib_hash_node_new). Intended to release the node structure without freeing the associated payload data. Exact handling of the key string is not documented in this header.
requirements: node must be a valid pointer to a gib_hash_node allocated by gib_hash_node_new or owned by a gib_hash instance.
Do not use the node after calling this function (use-after-free).
Associated payload data is not freed by this function; callers must manage it separately.
Behavior for node == NULL is not specified.

functions.name: gib_hash_node_free_and_data
functions.description: Frees a gib_hash_node and also frees its associated payload data. Use when the node’s data was heap-allocated and should be released together with the node. Exact treatment of the key string is not specified in this header.
requirements: node must be a valid pointer to a gib_hash_node.
The node’s associated data must be safe to free using the standard deallocator (malloc-compatible), and must not be freed elsewhere.
Do not use the node or its data after calling this function.
Behavior for node == NULL is not specified.

functions.name: gib_hash_new
functions.description: Creates and returns a new, empty gib_hash instance.
requirements: Returned hash must be freed with gib_hash_free or gib_hash_free_and_data to avoid memory leaks.

requirements: hash must be a valid pointer previously returned by gib_hash_new.
All entry payload data will remain allocated; the caller is responsible for freeing or otherwise managing it before or after this call as appropriate.
Do not use the hash after calling this function.

All stored payload data must be safe to free using the standard deallocator (malloc-compatible) and must not be freed elsewhere.

requirements: pms must be a non-null pointer to writable md5_state_t storage.

requirements: pms must be a non-null pointer to an md5_state_t that has been initialized with md5_init (inferred from API pattern).

May be called after zero or more md5_append calls (inferred).
After finalization, the state is no longer valid for appending the same message; to hash another message, call md5_init again (inferred).
The environment must support 8-bit chars and 32-bit ints, per header comment.

import string
from typing import List

# Data type: generic C string (NTBS). We will generate diverse, valid strings
# to exercise callers that expect names, labels, keys, paths, delimiters, etc.
# Target stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME; we provide a single
# bytes buffer that the harness will consume sequentially to satisfy those.
# Strategy:
# - Encode a compact header with a selection of patterns to cover:
#   - Mixed ASCII, punctuation, spaces
#   - URL-like strings
#   - File-like paths (absolute, relative)
#   - Short delimiters (including multi-char)
#   - Repeated tokens for split()
#   - Long-ish payload for hash/set payload fill
# - All fields are NUL-terminated to be usable as C strings, concatenated.
# - Limit total size to <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Helper generators for interesting strings

def rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Include letters, digits, punctuation, and spaces
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.:/@#%+?=&,;[](){}!$^~"
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def rand_delim(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Favor short, non-empty delimiters, occasionally multi-character
    choices = [",", "|", ";", ":", "/", "\\", "::", ",,", "--", "\t", " "]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(choices)
    # Random 1-4 length from punctuation
    punct = ",|;:/\\\t "
    ln = rng.randint(1, 4)
    return "".join(rng.choice(punct) for _ in range(ln))

def rand_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix absolute/relative, with directories and extensions
    exts = ["png", "jpg", "jpeg", "gif", "bmp", "txt", "dat", "bin"]
    parts = []
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append("/")
    depth = rng.randint(0, 4)
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(rand_ascii(rng, 1, 8))
    base = rand_ascii(rng, 1, 12)
    ext = rng.choice(exts)
    name = base + "." + ext
    path = "/".join([p for p in parts if p] + [name])
    if not path:
        path = name
    return path

def rand_url(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    schemes = ["http", "https", "ftp", "file"]
    host = rand_ascii(rng, 3, 10).lower()
    tld = rng.choice(["com", "org", "net", "io", "local"])
    path = "/" + rand_ascii(rng, 0, 8)
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        q = "?" + rand_ascii(rng, 1, 10)
    else:
        q = ""
    return f"{rng.choice(schemes)}://{host}.{tld}{path}{q}"

    # Ensure no embedded NUL; remove them if present and terminate with single NUL
    s = s.replace("\x00", "")
    return s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore') + b"\x00"

import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces a text buffer that is intended to be consumed by
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls in the gib_string_split fuzzer stub.
# The stub calls FUZZ_PARAM_STR() twice: once for the input string and once for
# the delimiter. Since we can only return a single bytes buffer, we encode both
# values into one buffer with a clear, simple header so the harness (or a
# pre-loader) can split them deterministically.
#
# Format (all ASCII text, newline separated):
#   DELIM:\n
#   <delimiter-bytes>\n
#   TEXT:\n
#   <payload-bytes>\n
# The delimiter is 1..8 bytes, non-empty. The payload (TEXT) is up to 256 bytes.
# The payload is constructed to contain a variety of token patterns so that
# different delimiters can exercise different paths in gib_string_split.

MAX_TEXT_LEN = 256
MAX_DELIM_LEN = 8

# Candidate interesting delimiters (1..8 bytes) including punctuation, spaces,
# multichar sequences, and mixed cases.
BASE_DELIMS = [
    ",", ";", " ", "\t", "|", ":", "/", "\\", ".", "-", "_",
    "::", "--", "||", "##", "@@", "==", "<>", "**", "++",
    "\r\n", "\n", "\r", "\x00",  # include NUL byte possibility (will be carried in bytes)
]

# Token pieces to assemble an interesting TEXT payload.
TOKENS = [
    "alpha", "beta", "gamma", "delta", "epsilon", "zeta",
    "one", "two", "three", "four", "five",
    "A", "B", "C", "D",
    "small", "BIG", "MiXeD",
    "",  # empty token to test consecutive delimiters
    "123", "0042", "10", "9",
    "ümlaut", "naïve", "café",  # UTF-8
    "path/to/file", "C\\\Windows\\System32",
    "a.b.c", "x-y-z",
]

# Surround tokens with potential leading/trailing delimiters to test edge cases.
EDGE_PREFIXES = ["", " ", "\t", "\n"]
EDGE_SUFFIXES = ["", " ", "\t", "\n"]


def _rand_delim(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Mix from base list and random printable bytes of variable length 1..8
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        d = rng.choice(BASE_DELIMS)
        # Allow generating multi-byte delimiter with random extension sometimes
        if 1 <= len(d) < MAX_DELIM_LEN and rng.random() < 0.2:
            extra_len = rng.randint(1, MAX_DELIM_LEN - len(d))
            d += ''.join(rng.choice(string.punctuation) for _ in range(extra_len))
        return d.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')
    # Random printable delimiter
    length = rng.randint(1, MAX_DELIM_LEN)
    # Allow including some whitespace and punctuation; avoid only-newline to keep variety
    alphabet = string.punctuation + string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " \t"
    d = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))
    # Ensure non-empty (guaranteed) and not purely whitespace sometimes
    if d.strip() == '' and length > 1:
        d = d[:-1] + rng.choice(string.punctuation)
    return d.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')


def _build_text_with_delim(rng: random.Random, delim: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Create a payload that contains a variety of token patterns.
    # We will join subsegments sometimes using the same delimiter to ensure hits,
    # and sometimes using other separators to create segments containing the delimiter.
    segments: List[str] = []

    # Decide number of segments
    n = rng.randint(5, 30)

    # A helper to maybe insert consecutive delimiters by adding empty tokens
    def maybe_empty():
        return '' if rng.random() < 0.25 else rng.choice(TOKENS)

    for _ in range(n):
        tok = maybe_empty()
        # Occasionally embed the delimiter bytes inside the token to verify that
        # multi-byte delimiters split only at exact matches.
        if rng.random() < 0.3 and len(delim) > 1:
            # Insert delim representation between random chars
            ins = delim.decode('utf-8', 'ignore')
            if not ins:
                ins = 'X'
            tok = tok + ins + rng.choice(TOKENS)
        # Optionally wrap with edge prefixes/suffixes
        tok = rng.choice(EDGE_PREFIXES) + tok + rng.choice(EDGE_SUFFIXES)
        segments.append(tok)

    # Join a portion of segments with the selected delimiter, and others with random glue
    text_parts: List[bytes] = []
    for i, s in enumerate(segments):
        text_parts.append(s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
        if i != len(segments) - 1:
            if rng.random() < 0.7:
                text_parts.append(delim)
            else:
                # random glue that is different from delim (best-effort)
                glue = _rand_delim(rng)
                if glue == delim:
                    glue += b"*"
                text_parts.append(glue)

    text = b''.join(text_parts)

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(text) > MAX_TEXT_LEN:
        text = text[:MAX_TEXT_LEN]

    # Ensure at least one occurrence of the delimiter in the text
    if delim not in text:
        # Insert delimiter at a random position
        pos = rng.randint(0, len(text))
        text = text[:pos] + delim + text[pos:]
        if len(text) > MAX_TEXT_LEN:
            text = text[:MAX_TEXT_LEN]

    return text


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a delimiter
    delim = _rand_delim(rng)
    # Avoid empty after encoding; enforce at least one byte
    if not delim:
        delim = b","  # fallback

    # Build text payload using this delimiter
    text = _build_text_with_delim(rng, delim)

    # Assemble the final buffer with a simple header so the harness can split.
    # Since FUZZ_PARAM_STR() in the stub independently supplies two strings, a
    # common setup is to feed the same initial bytes to both and the harness will
    # peel off the first (delimiter) and second (text) parts. Here we encode both
    # explicitly; consumers can parse accordingly.
    # Note: We include raw bytes; lines are separated using a sentinel header
    # that is ASCII and should not collide with typical delimiters.
    out = bytearray()
    out += b"DELIM:\n"
    out += delim + b"\n"
    out += b"TEXT:\n"
    out += text + b"\n"

    # Keep under 4096 bytes
    if len(out) > 4096:
        del out[4096:]

    return bytes(out)

# Target data type: binary blob
# We craft byte buffers that are valid inputs for the provided fuzz stubs when
# consumed via FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME-backed file contents.
# Strategy:
# - Generate small curated structures useful across the stubs:
#   * C-string friendly segments (ASCII, with and without NULs inside)

#   * MD5-friendly random blocks (varied lengths including 0)
#   * Key/value-like chunks for gib_hash_set / gib_hash_node_new
# - The returned buffer is a concatenation of segments, each prefixed by a tag
#   and length, so that the harness extracting FUZZ_PARAM_STR slices can find
#   interesting data across the buffer. Even if the harness takes arbitrary
#   substrings, including NULs and binary data increases valid coverage.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

PNG_SIG = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\x0a"

ASCII = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_-/."


def _rand_ascii(rnd: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    l = rnd.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return bytes(rnd.choice(ASCII) for _ in range(l))

    l = rnd.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return rnd.randbytes(l)


def _c_string_like(rnd: random.Random, base: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Ensure it is NUL-terminated to be a valid C string when needed
    # Also optionally inject interior NULs sometimes to test robustness,
    # but still end with a NUL terminator.
    b = bytearray(base)
    if len(b) > 4 and rnd.random() < 0.3:
        # insert an interior NUL
        pos = rnd.randrange(1, len(b)-1)
        b[pos] = 0
    if not b or b[-1] != 0:

    return bytes(b)

    # Simple TLV: tag(1) + length(2, big-endian) + payload

            # Non-PNG: random ascii/binary
            if rnd.random() < 0.5:
                out += _segment(b"p", _rand_ascii(rnd, 1, 48))
            else:
                out += _segment(b"p", _rand_binary(rnd, 1, 48))
    return bytes(out)


def _make_hash_material(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create keys and payloads suitable for gib_hash_node_new / gib_hash_set
    out = bytearray()
    # Some human-readable keys
    keys = [
        b"key",
        b"filename",
        b"user:name",
        b"/tmp/test.png",
        b"http://example.com/image.png",
    ]
    # Random keys
    for _ in range(5):
        keys.append(_rand_ascii(rnd, 3, 24))
    rnd.shuffle(keys)
    for k in keys:
        ckey = _c_string_like(rnd, k)
        # Data payload: small binary buffers (malloc-safe content)
        data = _rand_binary(rnd, 1, 128)
        out += _segment(b"K", ckey)
        out += _segment(b"D", data)
    return bytes(out)


def _make_md5_blocks(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Multiple blocks including zero-length, small and larger to append
    out = bytearray()
    sizes = [0, 1, 16, 63, 64, 65]
    # Add a few random sizes up to 1024 (the stub caps per-call to 1024)
    for _ in range(3):
        sizes.append(rnd.randint(2, 256))
    for sz in sizes:
        if sz == 0:
            payload = b""
        else:
            # Mix ASCII and binary for variety
            if rnd.random() < 0.5:
                payload = _rand_ascii(rnd, sz, sz)
            else:
                payload = _rand_binary(rnd, sz, sz)
        out += _segment(b"M", payload)
    return bytes(out)


def _make_colors_and_formats(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Useful for color parsing, file format strings, etc.
    out = bytearray()
    colors = [b"#000", b"#FFF", b"#112233", b"rgba(10,20,30,128)", b"red", b"blue"]
    for c in colors:
        out += _segment(b"C", _c_string_like(rnd, c))
    # Common image format names to help gib_imlib_image_format paths
    for name in [b"png", b"jpeg", b"jpg", b"gif", b"bmp", b"tiff"]:
        out += _segment(b"F", _c_string_like(rnd, name))
    return bytes(out)


def _truncate(buf: bytes, limit: int = 4096) -> bytes:
    return buf[:limit]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    parts = []
    # PNG-like and non-PNG blobs for filename-backed usage
    parts.append(_make_png_like_files(rnd))
    # Hash keys and data payloads
    parts.append(_make_hash_material(rnd))
    # MD5 append blocks
    parts.append(_make_md5_blocks(rnd))
    # Colors and formats as C-strings
    parts.append(_make_colors_and_formats(rnd))
    # Additional generic C-strings that look like paths/URLs
    for base in [
        b"/tmp/a.png", b"/var/tmp/out.jpg", b"C:/images/pic.bmp", b"file:///home/user/img.gif",
        b"http://host/path/img.png", b"https://host/a/b/c.jpeg",
    ]:
        parts.append(_segment(b"S", _c_string_like(rnd, base)))

    # Mix in some arbitrary binary to ensure variety
    parts.append(_segment(b"B", _rand_binary(rnd, 32, 128)))

    buf = b"".join(parts)
    return _truncate(buf)

import random

from typing import List

# We generate valid filesystem paths and generic strings for the fuzz stubs.
# Output: concatenation of NUL-terminated C-strings. Size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_."


def _rand_clean_name(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 16) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_ext(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice([".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".gif", ".bmp", ".txt", ".dat", ""])


def _random_text(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 8, max_len: int = 64) -> str:
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-:/.,+@#%[](){}"
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _build_paths_and_files(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Directory-like prefixes for feh_unique_filename
    dir_prefixes = [
        "/tmp/feh_fuzz_" + _rand_clean_name(rng, 4, 10),
        "/var/tmp/feh_" + _rand_clean_name(rng, 4, 8),
        "./out_" + _rand_clean_name(rng, 3, 6),
    ]

    files = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        base = _rand_clean_name(rng, 3, 12) + _rand_ext(rng)
        parent = rng.choice(["/tmp", "/var/tmp", ".", "./sub", "/tmp/feh_data"])
        path = parent + "/" + base
        files.append(path)

    # Include one path with a space
    files.append("/tmp/with space/" + _rand_clean_name(rng, 3, 8) + _rand_ext(rng))

    all_paths = dir_prefixes + files

    for p in all_paths:
        parts.append(p.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    return parts


def _build_generic_strings(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    out: List[bytes] = []

    # Font path-like strings for gib_imlib_parse_fontpath
    fontpaths = [
        "/usr/share/fonts:/usr/local/share/fonts",
        "~/.fonts:/usr/share/fonts/truetype",
        "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu:/usr/share/fonts/opentype",
    ]
    out.extend(s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00" for s in fontpaths)

    # Clean basenames for feh_unique_filename
    for _ in range(3):
        out.append(_rand_clean_name(rng, 1, 12).encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    # A few random general-purpose strings
    for _ in range(5):
        out.append(_random_text(rng, 4, 48).encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    return out


def _assemble_bundle(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Paths first
    parts.extend(_build_paths_and_files(rng))

    # Separator marker (still a C-string)
    parts.append(b"--sep--\x00")

    # Generic strings
    parts.extend(_build_generic_strings(rng))

    blob = b"".join(parts)
    if len(blob) > MAX_TOTAL:
        blob = blob[:MAX_TOTAL]
        if blob and blob[-1] != 0:
            blob = blob.rstrip(b"\x00") + b"\x00"
    return blob


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return _assemble_bundle(rng)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: font name (as understood by Imlib2/font backends)
# Goal: Produce bytes that represent interesting, valid font name strings.
# These will feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR in two stubs that attempt to load fonts.
# Strategy:
# - Generate a mix of common family names likely present on many systems.
# - Include style/weight/size variants (both X Logical Font Description (XLFD)-like
#   and Fontconfig-like descriptors) that Imlib2 commonly accepts.
# - Include UTF-8 family names to exercise parsing of non-ASCII.
# - Include numeric sizes, pixel sizes, and ranges within typical bounds.
# - Keep under 128 chars (the stub truncates to 128 anyway) and overall under 4096.
# - Always return a single null-terminated-friendly byte sequence (no embedded NULs).

COMMON_FAMILIES = [
    # Very common sans/serif/mono
    "Sans", "Serif", "Monospace",
    # De facto common fonts
    "DejaVu Sans", "DejaVu Serif", "DejaVu Sans Mono",
    "Liberation Sans", "Liberation Serif", "Liberation Mono",
    "Ubuntu", "Noto Sans", "Noto Serif", "Noto Sans Mono",
    "Arial", "Times New Roman", "Courier New",
    # X11 bitmap/100dpi/75dpi families typically seen on test machines
    "fixed", "Helvetica", "Times", "Courier", "Lucida",
]

# Some localized/Unicode family names commonly available in Noto collections
UNICODE_FAMILIES = [
    "Noto Sans CJK SC",  # Simplified Chinese
    "Noto Sans CJK JP",  # Japanese
    "Noto Sans CJK KR",  # Korean
    "DejaVu Sans",       # safe fallback with ASCII but we will add unicode style
    "Noto Color Emoji",
]

STYLES = ["Regular", "Bold", "Italic", "Bold Italic", "Oblique", "Light", "Medium", "SemiBold", "Black"]
WEIGHTS = ["thin", "extralight", "light", "book", "regular", "medium", "semibold", "bold", "extrabold", "black"]
SLANTS = ["r", "i", "o"]  # roman, italic, oblique in X logical naming
WIDTHS = ["normal", "condensed", "expanded"]

# Fontconfig-style patterns components
FC_KEYS = [
    "style", "weight", "slant", "width", "spacing", "dpi", "hintstyle", "antialias"
]

# XLFD template pieces (not full 14-field, but common shorthand or subsets)
XLFD_FOUNDRIES = ["", "misc", "adobe", "bitstream", "monotype", "ibm"]
XLFD_REGISTRIES = ["iso8859-1", "iso10646-1", "koi8-r", "jisx0208.1983-0"]

EMOJI = ["😀", "🄰", "𝘈", "𝔄", "Ａ", "é", "ä", "ç", "Ω", "漢"]


def rnd_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def make_simple_family(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    fam = rnd_choice(rng, COMMON_FAMILIES)
    # 50% add a size
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        size = rng.randint(6, 64)
        fam = f"{fam}/{size}"
    # 40% add a style suffix
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        fam = f"{fam} {rnd_choice(rng, STYLES)}"
    return fam


def make_fontconfig_pattern(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    fam = rnd_choice(rng, COMMON_FAMILIES + UNICODE_FAMILIES)
    parts = [fam]
    # Add colon-separated key=value pairs
    # A small number of attributes to keep it valid-ish
    kcount = rng.randint(1, 4)
    used = set()
    for _ in range(kcount):
        key = rnd_choice(rng, [k for k in FC_KEYS if k not in used])
        used.add(key)
        if key == "style":
            val = rnd_choice(rng, STYLES)
        elif key == "weight":
            val = rnd_choice(rng, WEIGHTS)
        elif key == "slant":
            val = rnd_choice(rng, ["roman", "italic", "oblique"]) 
        elif key == "width":
            val = rnd_choice(rng, WIDTHS)
        elif key == "spacing":
            val = rnd_choice(rng, ["proportional", "monospace"])
        elif key == "dpi":
            val = str(rng.choice([72, 96, 120, 144]))
        elif key == "hintstyle":
            val = rnd_choice(rng, ["hintnone", "hintslight", "hintmedium", "hintfull"])
        elif key == "antialias":
            val = rnd_choice(rng, ["true", "false", "1", "0"])
        else:
            val = "regular"
        parts.append(f"{key}={val}")
    # Optional size at end with :pixelsize= or :size=
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(f"size={rng.randint(6, 72)}")
        else:
            parts.append(f"pixelsize={rng.randint(6, 96)}")
    return ":".join(parts)


def make_xlfd_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Construct a reasonable XLFD-like name; Imlib2 often accepts subsets
    foundry = rnd_choice(rng, XLFD_FOUNDRIES)
    family = rnd_choice(rng, COMMON_FAMILIES).replace(" ", "-")
    weight = rnd_choice(rng, ["medium", "bold", "regular", "black", "light"])
    slant = rnd_choice(rng, ["r", "i", "o"])
    setwidth = rnd_choice(rng, ["normal", "condensed", "expanded"]) 
    addstyle = "-"  # often blank
    pixel = str(rng.randint(6, 64))
    point = str(rng.randint(60, 640))  # decipoints
    resx = str(rng.choice([72, 75, 96, 100]))
    resy = resx
    spacing = rnd_choice(rng, ["p", "m", "c"])  # proportional/monospace/charcell
    avgwidth = str(rng.randint(50, 200))
    registry = rnd_choice(rng, XLFD_REGISTRIES)
    parts = [foundry, family, weight, slant, setwidth, addstyle, pixel, point, resx, resy, spacing, avgwidth, registry]
    # Ensure foundry not empty placeholder at position 0 in real XLFD: use '*' if empty
    if parts[0] == "":
        parts[0] = "*"
    return "-" + "-".join(parts)


def make_unicode_variant(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    fam = rnd_choice(rng, UNICODE_FAMILIES)
    # sprinkle some unicode style markers
    deco = "".join(rng.choices(EMOJI, k=rng.randint(1, 3)))
    base = f"{fam} {rnd_choice(rng, STYLES)}"
    # optionally add a size
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        base += f" {rng.randint(8, 48)}"
    # insert decoration either prefix, infix or suffix
    mode = rng.randint(0, 2)
    if mode == 0:
        s = f"{deco} {base}"
    elif mode == 1:
        s = f"{base} {deco}"
    else:
        s = f"{fam} {deco} {rnd_choice(rng, STYLES)}"
    return s


def make_random_family(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Random synthetic family name that still looks plausible
    syll = ["no", "to", "sa", "ri", "ve", "li", "ber", "a", "mo", "no", "spa", "ce", "lu", "ci", "da"]
    n = rng.randint(2, 4)
    name = "".join(rng.choices(syll, k=n)).title()
    # End with known word to increase chance of fallback matching
    tail = rnd_choice(rng, [" Sans", " Serif", " Mono", " Pro", " UI"])
    base = name + tail
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base += f" {rnd_choice(rng, STYLES)}"
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        base += f" {rng.randint(7, 64)}"
    return base


def pick_generator(rng: random.Random):
    gens = [
        make_simple_family,
        make_fontconfig_pattern,
        make_xlfd_like,
        make_unicode_variant,
        make_random_family,
    ]
    return rnd_choice(rng, gens)


def sanitize(s: str) -> str:
    # Ensure it's within the stub's limit and contains no NULs
    s = s.replace("\x00", " ")
    # Trim whitespace extremes
    s = s.strip()
    # Truncate conservatively to 120 to leave headroom for encodings
    if len(s) > 120:
        s = s[:120]
    if not s:
        s = "Sans"
    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Weighted selection to favor simple valid names but still explore patterns
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.35:
        s = make_simple_family(rng)
    elif choice < 0.60:
        s = make_fontconfig_pattern(rng)
    elif choice < 0.75:
        s = make_xlfd_like(rng)
    elif choice < 0.90:
        s = make_unicode_variant(rng)
    else:
        s = make_random_family(rng)
    s = sanitize(s)
    # Return UTF-8 bytes
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    # Ensure under global limit
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
    return b

import random
import string

# This generator targets printf-style format string consumers in weprintf fuzzer stub.
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR will read from this buffer to produce an interesting string.
# We provide a mix of safe literal strings, strings with valid printf specifiers,
# edge-case wide/UTF-8 text, long runs, and embedded NULs near the end to test truncation.

MAX_LEN = 4096

SAFE_FORMATS = [
    "hello world",
    "%s",
    "%d",
    "%i",
    "%u",
    "%x",
    "%o",
    "%ld",
    "%zu",
    "%p",
    "%c",
    "mix-%s-%d",
    "%s %s",
    "literal 100%% done",  # escaped percent
    "[%10s] %04d",
    "%-12s:%+08d",
    "%s %d %x",
    "%s\n",
]

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "😀😃😄😁😆",
    "Русский текст",
    "日本語テキスト",
    "العَرَبِيَّة",
    "ευχαριστώ",
    "mañana café",
]

WORDS = [
    "alpha","beta","gamma","delta","epsilon","zeta","eta","theta",
    "iota","kappa","lambda","mu","nu","xi","omicron","pi","rho",
    "sigma","tau","upsilon","phi","chi","psi","omega",
]


def rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
    return ''.join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(n))


def make_valid_printf_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a string with specifiers that are safe for the fuzzer stub: %s and %d
    parts = []
    count = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(count):
        choice = rng.randint(0, 4)
        if choice == 0:
            parts.append("%s")
        elif choice == 1:
            parts.append("%d")
        elif choice == 2:
            # width/pad variants still compatible with %d
            parts.append(rng.choice(["%04d", "%+8d", "%-6d", "%10d"]))
        elif choice == 3:
            parts.append(rng.choice(["mix-%s-%d", "[%10s] %04d"]))
        else:
            # plain text token
            parts.append(rng.choice(WORDS))
    # Join with separators ensuring not to create stray % without specifier
    sep = rng.choice([" ", "-", "_", ":", " | "])
    s = sep.join(parts)
    # occasionally append a newline or escaped percent
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        s += rng.choice(["\n", " ", " 100%%"])  # 100%% becomes literal percent
    return s


def with_embedded_nul(rng: random.Random, s: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Insert a NUL near the middle or near the end to test C-string termination handling
    if not s:
        return b"\x00"
    pos = rng.randint(0, min(len(s), 64)) if rng.random() < 0.5 else max(0, len(s) - rng.randint(1, 16))
    return s[:pos] + b"\x00" + s[pos:]


def assemble_pool(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a pool of strings separated by newlines so FUZZ_PARAM_STR can slice diverse segments
    items = []

    # 1) Safe predefined formats
    items.extend(SAFE_FORMATS)

    # 2) Random valid printf-like strings focusing on %s and %d
    for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 10)):
        items.append(make_valid_printf_like(rng))

    # 3) Plain ASCII and long runs
    items.append(rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(8, 64)))
    items.append("A" * rng.randint(1, 256))

    # 4) Unicode samples
    items.extend(rng.sample(UNICODE_SAMPLES, k=rng.randint(1, min(3, len(UNICODE_SAMPLES)))))

    # 5) Path/URL-like strings which may show up in warnings
    items.extend([
        "/tmp/test.png",
        "http://example.com/image.jpg",
        "C:/Windows/Temp/log.txt",
        "../relative/path",
    ])

    # 6) Edge-case numeric text
    items.extend([
        str(0), str(-1), str(2**31 - 1), str(-2**31), str(10**9),
    ])

    # Join with newlines
    blob = "\n".join(items)
    data = blob.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')

    # Occasionally inject an embedded NUL to exercise C-string termination
    if rng.random() < 0.5 and len(data) < MAX_LEN - 1:
        data = with_embedded_nul(rng, data)

    # Ensure size bound
    return data[:MAX_LEN]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    buf = assemble_pool(rng)
    # Ensure non-empty
    if not buf:
        return b"test\n"
    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target: generate a small "separator string" suitable for estrjoin(sep, ...)
# The fuzzer stub bounds the separator to <=16 bytes and expects a valid C string.
# We return bytes that represent interesting but valid separators to trigger diverse paths
# in string joining (empty, single char, multi-char, whitespace, punctuation, UTF-8 sequences, etc.).

_MAX_LEN = 16

_ASCII_SETS = [
    "",                          # empty separator
    " ",                         # single space
    "\t",                        # tab
    "\n",                        # newline
    ",",                         # comma
    ":",                         # colon
    ";",                         # semicolon
    "|",                         # pipe
    "/",                         # slash
    "\\",                        # backslash
    "-",                         # dash
    "_",                         # underscore
    ".",                         # dot
    "::",                        # double colon
    " -- ",                      # spaced dashes
    " | ",                       # spaced pipe
    " • ",                       # bullet with spaces (UTF-8)
    " → ",                       # arrow (UTF-8)
    " — ",                       # em dash (UTF-8)
    "🙂",                        # emoji (UTF-8)
    "\x00",                      # contains NUL (will terminate early in C, interesting behavior)
]

# Additional generators to create random separators within valid ranges.
_DEF_PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "

_UTF8_CHOICES = [
    "α", "β", "γ", "Ω",          # Greek
    "ä", "ö", "ü", "ß",          # Latin-1
    "猫", "犬", "山",               # CJK
    "😀", "🚀", "✨",             # emoji
]

def _rand_printable(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(_DEF_PRINTABLE) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_utf8(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # mix ASCII and UTF-8 multibyte
    parts: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(n):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(rng.choice(_DEF_PRINTABLE))
        else:
            parts.append(rng.choice(_UTF8_CHOICES))
    return "".join(parts)

def _maybe_repeat(rng: random.Random, s: str, max_total: int) -> str:
    if not s:
        return s
    reps = rng.randint(1, max(1, max_total // max(1, len(s))))
    return (s * reps)[:max_total]

def _maybe_embed_nul(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Occasionally insert a NUL inside to explore early-termination behaviors in C.
    if not s or rng.random() < 0.6:
        return s
    pos = rng.randint(0, len(s))
    return s[:pos] + "\x00" + s[pos:]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a strategy bucket to diversify outputs across seeds
    strategy = rng.choices(
        population=[
            "predefined",
            "printable_short",
            "printable_long",
            "utf8_short",
            "utf8_long",
            "repeat_unit",
            "punct_run",
            "spaces",
            "tabs",
            "mixed_ws",
            "with_nul",
        ],
        weights=[20, 12, 10, 10, 8, 8, 7, 5, 5, 5, 10],
        k=1,
    )[0]

    if strategy == "predefined":
        s = rng.choice(_ASCII_SETS)
    elif strategy == "printable_short":
        s = _rand_printable(rng, 1, min(4, _MAX_LEN))
    elif strategy == "printable_long":
        s = _rand_printable(rng, 5, _MAX_LEN)
    elif strategy == "utf8_short":
        s = _rand_utf8(rng, 1, 4)
    elif strategy == "utf8_long":
        # ensure we cap to _MAX_LEN bytes after encoding, so build longer then trim
        s = _rand_utf8(rng, 3, 8)
    elif strategy == "repeat_unit":
        unit = rng.choice(["-", "_", "*", ".", ":", "|", " / ", " :: "])
        s = _maybe_repeat(rng, unit, _MAX_LEN)
    elif strategy == "punct_run":
        puncts = "".join(rng.choice(string.punctuation) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)))
        s = puncts
    elif strategy == "spaces":
        s = " " * rng.randint(1, _MAX_LEN)
    elif strategy == "tabs":
        s = "\t" * rng.randint(1, min(8, _MAX_LEN))
    elif strategy == "mixed_ws":
        ws = [" ", "\t", "\n"]
        s = "".join(rng.choice(ws) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, _MAX_LEN)))
    elif strategy == "with_nul":
        base = rng.choice([",", ":", "::", "|", " ", "--", "sep"])  # short base
        s = _maybe_embed_nul(rng, base,)
    else:
        s = ","

    # Occasionally embed a NUL regardless of strategy to cover that behavior
    if strategy not in ("with_nul",) and rng.random() < 0.15:
        s = _maybe_embed_nul(rng, s)

    # Ensure the encoded byte length does not exceed 16 bytes, per fuzzer cap
    # We trim by bytes to keep C-string size within bound while preserving valid UTF-8 prefix.
    b = s.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    if len(b) > _MAX_LEN:
        b = b[:_MAX_LEN]
        # Ensure we don't cut a multibyte sequence improperly: backtrack to a valid start
        # Valid UTF-8 leading byte patterns: 0xxxxxxx, 110xxxxx, 1110xxxx, 11110xxx
        # Continuation byte pattern: 10xxxxxx (0x80-0xBF). Remove trailing continuation bytes.
        while b and (b[-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
            b = b[:-1]

    # Always return a valid bytes buffer (may be empty). No mutation beyond selection.
    return b

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: filename
# Description: A base filename component (no path separators), suitable for
# constructing or combining into a full path.
#
# Target fuzzers use FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() for paths and FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for a basename.
# Our buffer should contain bytes that the harness will interpret as initial seed data
# for both calls. Since we cannot control the harness directly, we aim to provide a
# self-describing blob with multiple newline-separated candidates so the fuzzer runtime
# can pick slices. We keep filenames portable and free of path separators.
#
# Strategy:
# - Emit several candidate base filenames without any '/' or '\\'.
# - Include varied extensions and edge cases (very short, max-length near 64, mixed cases,
#   unicode-ish ASCII, spaces, dots, leading dot, many dots, numeric-only, with common
#   image extensions to exercise image-related code paths).
# - Also include directory-like names (but still no separators) that look like stems.
# - Ensure total size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# The result is a bytes blob with lines of candidate names. The fuzzer stubs sanitize the
# basename and use FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() for directories; common fuzzing frameworks split
# or sample from provided buffer. Providing many clean candidates increases valid coverage.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_. +@#()[]{}!$%^&=,;"  # no slashes or backslashes
IMAGE_EXTS = [
    "jpg", "jpeg", "png", "gif", "bmp", "tiff", "tif", "webp", "pnm", "ppm",
    "pgm", "pbm", "svg", "heic", "ico", "pcx"
]

def _rand_base(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # avoid NUL and separators; ensure not empty
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
    # Avoid trailing spaces only (some consumers may trim), but still valid
    if s.endswith(' '):
        s = s[:-1] + '_'
    # Ensure it doesn't start with a dash that some tools treat as option; still valid filename
    if s.startswith('-'):
        s = 'x' + s[1:]
    # Ensure not entirely dots to avoid special names
    if set(s) == {'.'}:
        s = 'x' + s
    return s

def _with_ext(name: str, ext: str) -> str:
    # If name already has an extension-like suffix, keep both by appending another.
    if name.endswith('.'):
        base = name[:-1]
    else:
        base = name
    return f"{base}.{ext}"

def _common_basenames() -> List[str]:
    return [
        "x", "a", "img", "image", "photo", "scan", "Screenshot", "thumbnail",
        "ICON", "cover", "album_art", "壁紙", "фото", "imagen", "测试", "테스트",
        ".hidden", "..dots..", "file", "untitled", "new file", "README.",
        "v1.0.0", "data_0001", "00000001", "NULfree", "space name",
    ]

def _interesting_names(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    names = []
    # Fixed interesting ones
    names.extend(_common_basenames())

    # Long near 64 chars
    long_core = ''.join('A' if i % 2 == 0 else 'a' for i in range(48))
    names.append(_with_ext(long_core, "png"))

    # Mixed punctuation
    names.append("img..v2..final")
    names.append("trailingdot.")
    names.append("leading.dot.name")
    names.append("multiple...dots")

    # Numeric heavy
    names.append("1234567890")
    names.append("2026-01-13_12-34-56")

    # Randomly generated batches
    for _ in range(20):
        base = _rand_base(rng, 1, 20)
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            base = _with_ext(base, rng.choice(IMAGE_EXTS))
        names.append(base)

    # Edge cases without extension
    for L in (1, 2, 3, 63, 64):
        nm = _rand_base(rng, L, L)
        names.append(nm)

    # Common image-like stems with common extensions
    for stem in ("IMG_0001", "DSC0001", "PXL_20260113_123456789", "scan_001", "cover@2x"):
        names.append(_with_ext(stem, rng.choice(IMAGE_EXTS)))

    # Ensure no path separators
    out = []
    for n in names:
        cleaned = n.replace('/', '_').replace('\\', '_')
        # Avoid empty and NULs
        cleaned = cleaned.replace('\x00', '')
        if not cleaned:
            cleaned = 'x'
        out.append(cleaned)
    return out

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    names = _interesting_names(rng)

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for n in names:
        if n not in seen:
            seen.add(n)
            uniq.append(n)

    # Append a few more random entries to diversify per-seed
    extra = []
    for _ in range(20):
        base = _rand_base(rng, 1, rng.randint(5, 32))
        if rng.random() < 0.8:
            base = _with_ext(base, rng.choice(IMAGE_EXTS))
        extra.append(base)
    for n in extra:
        n = n.replace('/', '_').replace('\\', '_').replace('\x00', '')
        if n and n not in seen:
            uniq.append(n)
            seen.add(n)

    # Join as newline-separated to offer many candidates. Keep <= 4096 bytes.
    blob = '\n'.join(uniq)
    b = blob.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
        # Ensure we don't cut in the middle of a multi-byte sequence or produce trailing partial line
        # Trim back to last newline if present
        cut = b.rfind(b'\n')
        if cut != -1:
            b = b[:cut]
    return b
